mainTopic: Working before holy days, incomes that lack סימן ברכה, and the binding force of local customs
overview: The משנה ends its rule on local customs: a person should not break from the local practice, because it causes מחלוקת. It adds a parallel case about carrying פירות שביעית between places, where the תנא קמא requires ביעור and רבי יהודה disagrees. The גמרא asks why the משנה singles out work on ערב פסח, since a ברייתא says work on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב from מנחה also brings no blessing. It answers that ערב פסח starts earlier (from חצות), or that on ערב פסח the worker can even receive שמתא. Related teachings follow: four types of people (diligent or lazy, rewarded or penalized), רבא on the women of מחוזא, and רבא's teaching that מצוות done שלא לשמה are still rewarded. A series of ברייתות then lists incomes that never see a סימן ברכה, ending with scribes and sellers of holy items, who do see blessing if they work לשמה. Finally, the גמרא returns to customs. רבי יוחנן rules that the children of בית שאן must keep their fathers' custom, and רב יוסף tells the people of חוזאי to drop their custom of taking חלה from rice. אביי begins a challenge to רב יוסף that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do not deviate from local custom
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes its rule about local customs: a person should not change from the local practice, because it leads to מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a person should not deviate from the local custom, because of dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its discussion of local customs, such as whether people work on ערב פסח until חצות. It gives the general principle: do not act differently from the local practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, the rule was that you follow the custom of the place you are in. This line gives the reason: acting differently from the people around you causes מחלוקת. Keeping the community together is a value in itself.

keyTerms.meaning: custom (the topic this line refers to)

phrases.english: And a person should not deviate
because of dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the earlier part of the משנה, which is not here, about following local custom on working on ערב פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may not break from local custom, because doing so causes מחלוקת.

steps.title: Moving Sabbatical-year produce between places
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a parallel case. Someone who carries פירות שביעית between a place where the crop is gone from the fields and a place where it is not must follow the stricter place and do ביעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, one who carries Sabbatical-year produce from a place where it has run out to a place where it has not run out, or from a place where it has not run out to a place where it has run out, is obligated to remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same idea: when you move between places with different rules, you must keep the stricter one. Here the case is about פירות שביעית and the obligation of ביעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית, you may keep the produce at home only while that species is still available in the fields. Once it is gone from the fields, you must do ביעור. The משנה rules that if either place has run out, the person must do ביעור, so he is held to the stricter of the two places.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה says both directions, from 'ran out' to 'not ran out' and the reverse. In both cases he must do ביעור, because he follows whichever place is stricter.

phrases.english: Similarly:
one who transports Sabbatical-year produce
from a place where they have run out
to a place where they have not run out,
or from a place where they have not run out
to a place where they have run out —
is obligated to remove them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel case to the principle of following the stricter local practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who moves פירות שביעית between places must do ביעור according to the stricter location.

steps.title: רבי יהודה disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the person does not need to do ביעור. He can tell a local resident: 'You too, go and bring some from the other place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Go out and bring for yourself too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the opposing view in the משנה. He holds that the person carrying the produce does not have to do ביעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reasons that the produce is still available somewhere, in the place where it has not run out. Anyone who complains can go there and get some too. So carrying it into the stricter place does not obligate him to do ביעור.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says to follow the stricter place and do ביעור. רבי יהודה says no ביעור is needed, because the produce is still available elsewhere.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Go out and bring for yourself, you too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling on ביעור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ביעור is required, since the produce is still available in the other place.

steps.title: Why single out ערב פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה discusses working on ערב פסח specifically. A ברייתא teaches that working on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב from מנחה onward also brings no blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically ערב פסח? Even ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב too! As it was taught: One who does work on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב from מנחה onward never sees a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It challenges the משנה's focus on ערב פסח, because a ברייתא shows that ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב have a similar problem with doing work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מאי איריא means 'why mention only this case?' The ברייתא shows that the concern about working before a holy day is not unique to פסח. So it seems the משנה should not have limited the topic to ערב פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the start of the Talmudic discussion
from the time of מנחה onward

phrases.english: GEMARA
Why specifically Passover eves?
Even Shabbat eves
and Festival eves as well!
As it was taught:
One who performs labor
on Shabbat eves and Festival eves
from Mincha time onward
never sees a sign of blessing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to question why the משנה limits the work issue to ערב פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's focus on working on ערב פסח specifically.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that working before שבת and יום טוב is also discouraged, so ערב פסח does not seem unique.

steps.title: First answer: ערב פסח starts earlier
steps.stepSummary: On ערב שבת the concern begins only from מנחה, and not just before it. On ערב פסח it begins earlier, from חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is from מנחה onward that it is forbidden; near מנחה, it is not. Here, it is from חצות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing out a difference in timing between ערב שבת and ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב שבת, work is a problem only once מנחה time has actually arrived. On ערב פסח, the restriction starts at חצות. This is earlier, because of the קרבן פסח, which was offered in the afternoon. So the משנה needed to teach ערב פסח separately.

phrases.english: There, from Mincha time onward
is when it is prohibited;
just before Mincha, not.
Here, it is from midday.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה הוּא דְּאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction in timing between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ערב פסח seemed to be the same as ערב שבת, so there was no reason to mention it.
steps.terutzMaskana: ערב פסח starts earlier, from חצות, so it needs its own ruling.

steps.title: Second answer: ערב פסח has a stronger penalty
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: on ערב שבת the worker only loses blessing, but nobody places him in שמתא. On ערב פסח he can even receive שמתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: There, it is only that he does not see a sign of blessing, but we do not excommunicate him. Here, we also excommunicate him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to answer the question. This time the difference is in how severe the penalty is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Working on ערב שבת is discouraged. The result is only that the work brings no blessing; it is not a formal prohibition. On ערב פסח it is a real איסור, so בית דין can place the person in שמתא. That stronger status is why the משנה mentions ערב פסח.
steps.whatToRemember: ערב פסח differs from ערב שבת in two possible ways: it starts earlier (from חצות), and it is a real איסור that can bring שמתא, not just a loss of blessing.

phrases.english: Alternatively:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, סִימָן בְּרָכָה הוּא דְּלָא חָזֵי,
phrases.english: there, it is a sign of blessing that he does not see,
but we do not excommunicate him.
Here, we also excommunicate him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 4, separate from step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערב שבת and ערב פסח cases seemed to have the same status.
steps.terutzMaskana: ערב פסח is a real איסור that can bring שמתא, while ערב שבת only loses blessing.

steps.title: The full ברייתא about working near holy days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the complete ברייתא. It adds working on מוצאי שבת, מוצאי יום טוב, מוצאי יום הכפורים, and any time with a hint of sin, such as a תענית ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: One who works on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב from מנחה onward, and on מוצאי שבת, מוצאי יום טוב, מוצאי יום הכפורים, and in any situation where there is a trace of sin, which includes a תענית ציבור, never sees a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the formula גופא ('the matter itself'), the גמרא goes back and quotes the full ברייתא that it only partly cited in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ברייתא adds the time right after holy days. Working at the very edge of a holy day risks slipping into real חילול. It also includes any time with a נדנוד עבירה, a slight hint of sin. The גמרא explains that this phrase comes to include a תענית ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': returning to quote a source in full

phrases.english: The matter itself:
One who performs labor
on Shabbat eves and on Festival eves
from Mincha time onward,
and at the conclusion of Shabbat and at the conclusion of a Festival
and at the conclusion of Yom Kippur,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם נִידְנוּד עֲבֵירָה,
phrases.english: and in any situation where there is a trace of sin,
which comes to include a public fast —
never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to quote in full the ברייתא that was partly cited in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working near the edges of holy days, or at times with a hint of sin such as a תענית ציבור, brings no blessing.

steps.title: Four types: diligent or lazy, rewarded or penalized
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sets up four categories of people: diligent and rewarded, diligent and penalized, lazy and rewarded, lazy and penalized.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There is one who is diligent and gains, and one who is diligent and loses. There is one who is lazy and gains, and one who is lazy and loses.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the theme of blessing from work, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with four categories. This step only lists them; the next step explains what each one means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprising point is that being diligent is not always good, and being lazy is not always bad. Whether a person gains or loses depends on when he works, as the next step will explain.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There is one diligent and rewarded,
and there is one diligent and penalized.
There is one lazy and rewarded,
and there is one lazy and penalized.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects by theme to the idea of blessing, or lack of it, from work near שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Diligence and laziness can each lead to gain or loss.

steps.title: Defining the four types
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the four types. The deciding factor is whether the person works on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Diligent and rewarded: works all week and does not work on ערב שבת. Diligent and penalized: works all week and works on ערב שבת. Lazy and rewarded: does not work all week and does not work on ערב שבת. Lazy and penalized: does not work all week and works on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now defines each of the four categories it just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Diligent' or 'lazy' describes how the person works during the week. 'Rewarded' or 'penalized' depends only on ערב שבת: if he works on ערב שבת, he loses. So working all week is good, but working into ערב שבת cancels the gain.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב שבת, the day before שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Here שבתא means 'week' in כולי שבתא, but מעלי שבתא means ערב שבת. Do not read כולי שבתא as 'all of שבת'.

phrases.english: Diligent and rewarded —
one who works the whole week,
and does not work on Shabbat eve.
Diligent and penalized —
one who works the whole week,
and works on Shabbat eve.
Lazy and rewarded —
one who does not work the whole week,
and does not work on Shabbat eve.
Lazy and penalized —
one who does not work the whole week,
and works on Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the four categories introduced in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working on ערב שבת leads to loss, and refraining from it leads to gain, regardless of how much one works during the week.

steps.title: רבא on the pampered women of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that the women of מחוזא, who do not work on ערב שבת only because they are pampered and never work, are still called 'lazy and rewarded'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These women of מחוזא, even though they do not work on ערב שבת, it is because of pampering, since they do not work on any day. Even so, we call them lazy and rewarded.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies the ברייתא to a real case. He rules that even people who rest on ערב שבת without a religious motive still get the 'rewarded' label.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the reward comes only when someone rests on ערב שבת out of respect for שבת. רבא teaches that the outcome itself, not working on ערב שבת, earns the reward, even when the reason is just luxury.

keyTerms.meaning: the women of מחוזא, a wealthy town

steps.whatToRemember: Not working on ערב שבת brings reward even when the motive is not pious. The result counts.

phrases.english: Rava said:
These women of Mechoza,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא עָבְדָן עֲבִידְתָּא
phrases.english: even though they do not do work
on Shabbat eve —
it is because of pampering,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא כׇּל יוֹמָא נָמֵי לָא קָא עָבְדָן.
phrases.english: since they do not work on any day either.
Even so —
we call them lazy and rewarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'lazy and rewarded' category from step 9 to a real case where the motive is not pious.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even rest on ערב שבת that comes from pampering earns the 'lazy and rewarded' label.

steps.title: Two verses about God's kindness seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that one פסוק says God's חסד reaches 'until the heavens' and another says 'above the heavens.' He asks how both can be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised a contradiction: One verse says 'Your kindness is great until the heavens,' and another says 'Your kindness is great above the heavens.' How can both be true?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets two nearly identical פסוקים side by side and shows they disagree on one word. He is setting up the question that his answer in the next step will solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse uses the word עד, meaning 'up to,' and the other uses מעל, meaning 'higher than.' That suggests two different levels of God's kindness. The question is when each level applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction (literally 'threw' two sources against each other)
How can this be? (a request to reconcile the sources)

phrases.english: Rava raised a contradiction:
It is written: "For Your kindness is great until the heavens,"
and it is written: "For Your kindness is great above the heavens."
How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of רבא's previous statement, that the women of מחוזא are rewarded even without a pious motive. It turns to reward for מצוות done without pure intent (לשמה versus שלא לשמה).
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the two פסוקים in תהלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same phrase gives two different heights for God's חסד, so the two verses seem to contradict.

steps.title: Resolution: לשמה versus שלא לשמה
steps.stepSummary: The 'above the heavens' verse is about people who do מצוות לשמה. The 'until the heavens' verse is about people who do them שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here the verse is speaking about those who do a מצוה for its own sake, and there it is speaking about those who do it not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own contradiction by giving each verse a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who does a מצוה purely for the sake of Heaven receives the greater kindness, 'above the heavens.' Someone with an ulterior motive still receives kindness, but at the lower level, 'until the heavens.' The point is that even the lower level is a real reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (pointing to one of the two verses)
For its own sake, with pure intent
Not for its own sake, with an ulterior motive

phrases.english: Here, it speaks of those who act for its own sake,
phrases.notes: This refers to the 'above the heavens' verse.

phrases.english: and here, of those who act not for its own sake.
phrases.notes: This refers to the 'until the heavens' verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each verse applies to a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses seem to describe one level of חסד in two conflicting ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two levels of reward. The higher one is for מצוות done לשמה and the lower one is for מצוות done שלא לשמה.

steps.title: Support from רב: keep learning even without pure motives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the idea that שלא לשמה is still rewarded with רב's statement that a person should always learn and do מצוות even שלא לשמה, because it leads to לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits with רב יהודה, who said in the name of רב: A person should always occupy himself with Torah and מצוות even not for their own sake, because from doing it not for its own sake he will come to do it for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רב to show that רבא's idea matches an accepted teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If doing a מצוה שלא לשמה were worthless, רב would not tell people to do it. רב says it is worthwhile because it is a path to לשמה. That fits רבא's claim that even the שלא לשמה level gets God's kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: Always (here it introduces a general life rule, not 'forever')

steps.whatToRemember: Even a מצוה done with mixed motives is rewarded, at a lower level. It is also the doorway to doing it purely לשמה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here לְעוֹלָם means 'always, as a rule,' not 'forever.' Later here the same word means 'ever,' as in 'never sees a sign of blessing.'
steps.whyThisMatters: רב's statement is a foundational rule in Jewish learning and practice. It is often quoted to encourage learning even when one's motives are not yet perfect.

phrases.english: And this is in line with Rav Yehuda.
For Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A person should always engage in Torah and מצוות
even if not for their own sake,
for out of doing it not for its own sake, he comes to do it for its own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 12 that שלא לשמה still earns reward.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a מצוה done שלא לשמה still receives God's kindness
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב: a person should always engage in Torah and מצוות even שלא לשמה

steps.title: No blessing from relying on a wife's or a mill's earnings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a man who counts on his wife's wages or on income from a mill will never see a סימן ברכה from that money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who looks forward to his wife's earnings or to earnings from a mill will never see a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a series of ברייתות about kinds of income that never show a סימן ברכה. This continues the 'blessing' theme from ערב שבת work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the rule but does not yet explain which 'wife's earnings' or which 'mill' it means. The next step defines both. The key word is הַמְצַפֶּה: the problem is depending on this small income.

keyTerms.meaning: One who looks forward to, relies on
A sign of blessing, visible success or growth

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who looks forward to the earnings of his wife or of a mill —
never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמְצַפֶּה לִשְׂכַר אִשְׁתּוֹ וְרֵיחַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new list of ברייתות about סימן ברכה, echoing the 'never sees a sign of blessing' theme of steps 4 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relying on a wife's wages or on mill income brings no visible blessing.

steps.title: Defining the wife's earnings and the mill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'wife's earnings' means spinning for others and being paid by weight on a scale, and 'mill' means renting out a hand mill.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His wife's earnings' means work paid by the scale. 'A mill' means renting it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies the two cases in the ברייתא so we know exactly what kind of income is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are tiny, piecemeal incomes. The wife is paid by the weight of thread she spins and has to go around looking for customers. The mill earns small rental fees. This sets up the contrast in the next step, where a different kind of work by a wife is praised.

keyTerms.meaning: A scale; here, work paid by weight

phrases.english: The earnings of his wife — by the scale.
phrases.notes: She spins thread for others and is paid by its weight (רבינו חננאל).

phrases.english: The mill — by rent.
phrases.notes: Others pay to grind their grain on his mill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two cases mentioned in the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cases with no blessing are a wife paid by weight and a mill rented out for small fees.

steps.title: A wife who makes and sells goods is praised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the ruling. If a wife makes products and sells them herself, the פסוק praises her for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if she makes goods and sells them, the verse praises her, as it says: 'She made a linen garment and sold it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that not all of a wife's work is included in the 'no blessing' rule. It proves this with a פסוק from אשת חיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was small piecework paid by the scale, not a wife earning money in general. When she produces finished goods and sells them, that is honorable work. משלי לא praises exactly that.

phrases.english: But if she makes goods and sells them —
the verse indeed praises her,
as it is written: "She made a linen garment and sold it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of steps 14–15 to piecework, and excludes a wife who makes and sells finished goods.
steps.raayaObject: A wife making and selling her own products is praiseworthy, not blessing-less

steps.title: No blessing from selling rods or jugs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who earns a living selling rods or clay jugs never sees a סימן ברכה from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who earns a living from rods and jugs never sees a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with a new kind of business that does not bring blessing. The reason comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new category: bulky merchandise. The ברייתא gives no reason, so the גמרא will ask for one right away.

keyTerms.meaning: One who earns a living, profits

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who earns a living from rods and jugs —
never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא in the same list of incomes without blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Income from selling rods and jugs brings no visible blessing.

steps.title: Reason: bulky goods attract the evil eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why selling rods and jugs brings no blessing. It answers that because they take up a lot of space, they draw עין הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since they are large in volume, the evil eye has power over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the previous ברייתא and answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rods and jugs are bulky, so a small stock looks like a big business. People think the seller is doing very well, and that envy, עין הרע, takes away the blessing.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since their volume is large —
the evil eye has power over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the ruling in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why selling rods and jugs brings no blessing
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their large volume makes the business look big, so עין הרע has power over it.

steps.title: Four kinds of people who never see blessing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four types who never see a סימן ברכה: alleyway merchants, raisers of small livestock, those who cut down good trees, and those who eye the best share.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Merchants in an alleyway, those who raise small livestock, those who cut down good trees, and those who set their eyes on the nice portion never see a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא with four more cases. The reason comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These four cases are very different from each other. Selling in a public alley, raising sheep and goats that graze in others' fields, chopping down fruit trees, and grabbing the best share are all conduct that people notice. The next step shows that this is the shared thread.

keyTerms.meaning: Merchants who sell in an alleyway beside a main road, in full view

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Merchants in an alleyway,
and those who raise small livestock,
phrases.notes: These animals tend to graze in and damage other people's fields.

phrases.english: and those who cut down good trees,
phrases.notes: Good fruit trees, even where cutting them is permitted.

phrases.english: and those who set their eyes on the nice portion —
phrases.notes: When dividing something with others, he aims to take the best part for himself.

phrases.english: never see a sign of blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third ברייתא in the list of incomes and behaviors without blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These four types of people never see a visible blessing in their earnings.

steps.title: Reason: people stare and wonder at them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why these four types lack blessing. It answers that people look at them and wonder about their conduct.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because people stare and wonder about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one reason that covers all four cases in the previous ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four behaviors make people take notice and talk about the person. That kind of public attention, with people wondering at what he is doing, keeps blessing from resting on what he earns.

keyTerms.meaning: They stare in wonder, are amazed

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because people stare and wonder about him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for all four cases in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why these four types of people lack blessing
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People stare at them and wonder about their conduct, and that attention removes the blessing.

steps.title: Four kinds of payment that never carry blessing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four kinds of money that never carry a סימן ברכה: wages of scribes, wages of מתורגמנין, money from orphans, and money that comes from overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There are four kinds of coins that never carry a sign of blessing: wages of scribes, wages of translators, earnings from orphans, and money that comes from overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a final ברייתא with four specific kinds of payment. The ברייתא gives no reasons here; the גמרא will explain them next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are not businesses like the earlier cases. They are particular sources of money. The scribes write holy books, the מתורגמנין explain the שבת lecture, the orphans' money is earned through a partnership with an orphans' estate, and the overseas money comes from far away. Each one is a different kind of source.

keyTerms.meaning: Speakers who repeat and explain the Sage's lecture to the public

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתות list incomes that never show a סימן ברכה. The themes include small or demeaning earnings, drawing עין הרע or people's stares, and certain specific sources of money.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע פְּרוּטוֹת אֵין בָּהֶן סִימָן בְּרָכָה לְעוֹלָם:
phrases.english: Four kinds of coins never have a sign of blessing in them:
the wages of scribes,
and the wages of translators,
phrases.notes: They repeat and explain the חכמים' שבת lectures.

phrases.english: and earnings from orphans,
phrases.notes: Profit from a partnership with an orphans' estate.

phrases.english: and money that comes from an overseas country.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, אַרְבַּע פְּרוּטוֹת אֵין בָּהֶן סִימָן בְּרָכָה לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth ברייתא in the list of incomes without blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wages of scribes, wages of מתורגמנין, earnings from orphans, and overseas money never carry a visible blessing.

steps.title: Explaining three of the four kinds of money that lack blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives reasons why the wages of מתורגמנין, money of orphans, and money from overseas carry no blessing. This sets up a question about the fourth item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the wages of מתורגמנין lack blessing because they look like שכר שבת. Orphans' money also lacks blessing, because orphans cannot forgive small losses. Money from overseas lacks blessing because a miracle does not happen every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains three of the four items from the ברייתא in Step 21. It is setting up the next move, a question about the one item that is still unexplained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתורגמן is mostly paid for work done on שבת, so his pay looks like שכר שבת. Orphans are minors and cannot legally forgive even tiny amounts, so any small overcharge counts as theft. Overseas trade is dangerous, so each safe arrival uses up a miracle and the merchant's merit.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this is understandable (opens a 'this part is fine, but...' setup)
Speakers who loudly explain the רב's lecture to the crowd
Payment for work done on שבת (forbidden)
Legally able to forgive or give up money

phrases.english: Granted, the wages of the disseminators:
because it looks like Shabbos wages.
phrases.notes: They mainly work at שבת lectures.

phrases.english: And orphans' money too:
they are not capable of forgiving.
phrases.notes: Minors cannot waive even small losses.

phrases.english: Money that comes from overseas:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו כׇּל יוֹמָא מִתְרְחִישׁ נִיסָּא.
phrases.english: because a miracle does not happen every day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives reasons for three of the four items listed in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why each kind of money lacks a סימן ברכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Looks like שכר שבת; orphans cannot forgive; overseas profit relies on miracles.

steps.title: Why do scribes' wages lack blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the remaining item, the wages of scribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the wages of scribes, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Having explained three items, the גמרא asks about the fourth. Writing holy items seems like good work, so it is not obvious why it would lack blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא completes the בשלמא setup: 'those three are clear, but this one is not.' A scribe does a מצוה, so the lack of blessing needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the item that is still difficult)

phrases.english: But the wages of scribes, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא structure by asking about the one unexplained item.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason scribes' wages carry no blessing.

steps.title: The Great Assembly fasted so scribes would not become rich
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that the אנשי כנסת הגדולה fasted 24 fasts so that scribes would not get rich. If scribes became rich, they would stop writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The men of the Great Assembly sat through twenty-four fasts for the writers of ספרים, תפילין, and מזוזות, that they should not become rich. If they became rich, they would no longer write.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about scribes. Their lack of wealth is on purpose, so that holy items keep being written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lack of blessing here is not a punishment. It comes from a deliberate prayer of the Sages for the public good. A rich scribe would quit, and the people would be left without ספרי תורה, תפילין, and מזוזות.

keyTerms.meaning: The Men of the Great Assembly (early חכמים of the בית שני era)
Writers of ספרי תורה, תפילין, and מזוזות

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean writing holy items is bad. The poverty is a deliberate safeguard so that scribes keep writing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Twenty-four fasts
the Men of the Great Assembly sat (observed)
for the writers of scrolls, tefillin, and mezuzos
that they should not become wealthy,
for if they would become wealthy, they would not write.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Sages fasted so that scribes would stay poor and keep writing.

steps.title: All who deal in holy work see no blessing unless they work for its sake
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא extends the idea. Scribes, their dealers, the dealers' dealers, and anyone in holy work, including sellers of תכלת, see no blessing. If they work לשמה, they do see blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Writers of ספרים, תפילין, and מזוזות, they, their dealers, their dealers' dealers, and everyone who works in heavenly work (this includes sellers of תכלת) never see a sign of blessing. But if they do it for its own sake, they do see blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that widens the group from scribes to everyone in the business of holy items. It then adds an important exception for those who work לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'all who engage in heavenly work' adds sellers of תכלת. The lack of blessing applies to someone treating holy work as plain business. Someone whose goal is to supply the public with מצוות does see blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own sake (for the sake of the מצוה)

steps.whatToRemember: Holy-item work done for profit lacks blessing, but the same work done לשמה brings blessing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Writers of scrolls, tefillin, and mezuzos,
they, and their merchants, and their merchants' merchants,
and all who engage in the work of Heaven,
to include sellers of tekhelet:
never see a sign of blessing.
But if they engage in it for its own sake, they do see blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כּוֹתְבֵי סְפָרִים תְּפִילִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and broadens רבי יהושע בן לוי's point about scribes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those in the business of holy items see no blessing unless they work לשמה.

steps.title: The children of בית שאן ask to drop their fathers' custom
steps.stepSummary: The people of בית שאן had a custom not to travel from צור to צידון on ערב שבת. Their children came to רבי יוחנן and said they could not afford to keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of בית שאן were accustomed not to go from צור to צידון on ערב שבת. Their children came before רבי יוחנן and said to him: For our fathers it was possible; for us it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, the force of local customs, which ties back to the משנה's rule about following local practice. The children ask רבי יוחנן whether they may stop a custom their fathers kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The custom was a stringency in honor of שבת. It was not required by הלכה. The children argue that their fathers were wealthy enough to skip Friday's market, but they need the income.

phrases.english: The people of Beit She'an were accustomed
not to go from Tyre to Sidon
on Shabbos eve.
Their children came before Rabbi Yochanan,
they said to him: For our fathers it was possible;
for us it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי בַיְישָׁן נְהוּג דְּלָא הֲווֹ אָזְלִין מִצּוֹר לְצִידוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: stories about the binding force of customs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether children may abandon a stringent custom their fathers accepted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules the fathers' custom binds the children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that their fathers already accepted the custom upon themselves. He brings the פסוק 'Hear, my son, your father's rebuke and do not forsake your mother's teaching.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Your fathers already accepted it upon themselves, as it says: 'Hear, my son, the rebuke of your father, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן refuses to cancel the custom. Because the fathers accepted it, the children are bound by it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as two layers. 'Your father's rebuke' is הלכה, and 'your mother's teaching' is the family's customs. A custom accepted by earlier generations becomes binding on later ones, even when keeping it is hard.
steps.whatToRemember: A מנהג accepted by one's fathers binds the next generation, based on 'ואל תטוש תורת אמך'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the binding force of inherited family and community customs.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּבָר קִיבְּלוּ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם עֲלֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: He said to them: Your fathers already accepted it upon themselves,
as it is stated: "Hear, my son, the rebuke of your father
and do not forsake the teaching of your mother."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּבָר קִיבְּלוּ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the children's request from Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The custom remains binding because the fathers accepted it, supported by משלי א:ח.

steps.title: רב יוסף tells them to break the custom of חלה from rice
steps.stepSummary: The people of חוזאי separated חלה from rice dough. רב יוסף said a non-כהן should eat it in front of them, to show the custom has no basis.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of חוזאי were accustomed to separate חלה from rice. They came and told רב יוסף. He said to them: Let a זר eat it in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second story about customs, with the opposite result. רב יוסף wants to publicly undo this custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rice is not one of the five grains, so rice dough has no obligation of חלה at all. Treating it as real חלה could mislead people, so רב יוסף wants a זר to eat it openly and show it has no holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.english: The people of Chozai were accustomed
to separate challah from rice,
they came and told Rav Yosef.
He said to them: Let a non-priest eat it in their presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי חוֹזָאֵי נָהֲגִי דְּמַפְרְשִׁי חַלָּה מֵאָרוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second custom story. Unlike רבי יוחנן, רב יוסף moves to cancel the custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-כהן should eat the 'חלה' publicly, showing the custom has no legal basis.

steps.title: אביי begins a challenge from permitted things treated as forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to challenge רב יוסף with a ברייתא about permitted things that people were accustomed to treat as forbidden. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised an objection to him: Things that are permitted, but others were accustomed to treat as forbidden...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins quoting a source to attack רב יוסף's ruling. The rest of the quote, and its point, comes next, so this line sets up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא deals with exactly this kind of case, where something is permitted but people treat it as forbidden. אביי will use it to argue that such a custom should not be openly broken in front of them.

keyTerms.meaning: They were accustomed to treat them as forbidden

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
Things that are permitted
but others were accustomed to treat them as forbidden...
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דְּבָרִים הַמּוּתָּרִים וַאֲחֵרִים נָהֲגוּ בָּהֶן אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling in Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's instruction to have a זר eat the rice 'חלה' in front of them.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about permitted things treated as forbidden seems to say such customs should not be openly broken (completed on the next amud).
